mechanism_narrative: A higher unemployment rate (UNRATE) reflects deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when UNRATE > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it signals an active monetary tightening cycle that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the months when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Weak housing market conditions (HOUST below 2000.0) combined with a high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) signal a dual stress on the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the months when HOUST < 2000.0 and FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monetary tightening cycle (defined as FEDFUNDS rising for 3 consecutive months) increases the cost of capital and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the periods when FEDFUNDS increases for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Higher housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong consumer demand and economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in less than 40% of months when HOUST > 2000.0.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 105.0, it signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which typically precedes economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the months when INDPRO < 105.0.

mechanism_narrative: Weak labor market growth (PAYEMS growth rate below 0.5% per month) combined with declining retail sales (RSAFS growth rate below 0.3% per month) signals a dual weakness in the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the months when PAYEMS growth < 0.5% and RSAFS growth < 0.3%.

mechanism_narrative: During a supply-side contraction (INDPRO below 105.0 and UNRATE above 5.0%), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to reduced economic output and rising unemployment, producing negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the months when INDPRO < 105.0 and UNRATE > 5.0.
